es: Comprender el estado de ánimo, el motivo y una expresión clave de un personaje a partir de sus acciones en un fragmento de cuento (texto y audio).

teaching.en: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends, and by the evening she has come to dread every conversation about results.
teaching.es: Mara se siente inquieta antes del examen, así que intenta evitar a sus amigos, y por la tarde ya teme cualquier conversación sobre las notas.
teaching.explanationEs: El ánimo (anxious) explica la acción (avoid) y dread nombra el miedo a lo que viene: del motivo a la conducta.
segments: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends,
and by the evening she has come to dread every conversation about results.
teaching.audioText: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends, and by the evening she has come to dread every conversation about results.

teaching.en: Leo is eager to start the project, but his sister looks reluctant, probably because she cannot forget how badly the last one ended.
teaching.es: Leo tiene muchas ganas de empezar el proyecto, pero su hermana parece reacia, probablemente porque no olvida lo mal que acabó el último.
teaching.explanationEs: Eager y reluctant son opuestos: muchas ganas frente a poca gana de hacer algo, y el texto suele dar la razón.
segments: Leo is eager to start the project, but his sister looks reluctant,
probably because she cannot forget how badly the last one ended.
teaching.audioText: Leo is eager to start the project, but his sister looks reluctant, probably because she cannot forget how badly the last one ended.

teaching.en: When the door finally opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him, and he could brush off the teasing that would certainly follow.
teaching.es: Cuando por fin se abrió la puerta, Tom se sintió aliviado: nadie lo había visto y podría quitar importancia a las burlas que seguramente vendrían.
teaching.explanationEs: Relieved es el ánimo de quien deja de preocuparse; had seen sitúa el hecho antes del alivio y brush off es restar importancia.
segments: When the door finally opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him,
and he could brush off the teasing that would certainly follow.
teaching.audioText: When the door finally opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him, and he could brush off the teasing that would certainly follow.

teaching.en: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother, and the longer she waited, the more sheepish she felt about picking up the phone.
teaching.es: Se sentía culpable porque no había llamado a su abuela, y cuanto más esperaba, más cohibida se sentía para contestar el teléfono.
teaching.explanationEs: Guilty + because da el motivo de la emoción con un hecho anterior (had not called); sheepish añade vergüenza.
segments: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother, and the longer
she waited, the more sheepish she felt about picking up the phone.
teaching.audioText: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother, and the longer she waited, the more sheepish she felt about picking up the phone.

teaching.en: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive, which he never admitted to anyone, was to say sorry.
teaching.es: Empezó a dudar ante la puerta, y su verdadero motivo, que nunca admitió ante nadie, era pedir perdón.
teaching.explanationEs: Hesitate es una acción que muestra el ánimo; motive es la razón que explica lo que hace.
segments: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive,
which he never admitted to anyone, was to say sorry.
teaching.audioText: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive, which he never admitted to anyone, was to say sorry.

teaching.en: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo, and that silence told the reader more than any adjective could have done.
teaching.es: No habló; solo siguió mirando fijamente la vieja foto, y ese silencio dijo al lector más de lo que habría dicho cualquier adjetivo.
teaching.explanationEs: Stare at es una acción sin palabras: el autor muestra el ánimo sin nombrarlo.
segments: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo,
and that silence told the reader more than any adjective could have done.
teaching.audioText: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo, and that silence told the reader more than any adjective could have done.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué explica mejor la conducta de Mara?

choices.text: She is eager to spend the week alone with her own thoughts.
She is relieved that her friends have finally stopped calling.
She is anxious about something she does not want to discuss.

feedback.es: Evitar a los amigos y contestar con una palabra sugiere inquietud ante algo que no quiere tratar, no ganas de estar sola.

hint.es: Fíjate en las acciones: ¿qué ánimo y qué motivo encajan con ellas?

origin.text: Mara has been avoiding her friends all week. She leaves the library when they come in, and she answers their messages with one word, if she answers at all.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom se sintió aliviado cuando se abrió la puerta.»

feedback.es: Relieved es el ánimo de quien deja de preocuparse al comprobar que no pasó lo temido.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de quien respira tranquilo después de una preocupación.

origin.text: Nobody had seen him. Tom felt ___ when the door opened, because he could finally stop worrying.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Siguió mirando fijamente la vieja foto.»

answer.text: She continued to stare at the old photo

feedback.es: Continue to + verbo base y stare at + objeto muestran una acción sostenida sin palabras.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y sigue con continued to.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué motiva a Leo a acercarse a la puerta de su hermana.

choices.text: He wants to apologise for selling her guitar.
He wants to ask her for a guitar lesson.
He wants to find out who took the guitar.

feedback.es: Leo vendió la guitarra sin preguntar y ha ensayado una disculpa: su motivo es pedir perdón.

origin.audio: Leo waited outside his sister's door for ten minutes. He raised his hand, lowered it, and stared at the handle as if it might bite. Two weeks earlier he had sold her old guitar without asking, and he had rehearsed his apology all the way home. When the door finally opened, Sara simply looked at him, and he forgot every word he had prepared.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere que Leo olvide sus palabras al final.

choices.text: Sara's angry words make him change his mind about apologising.
He feels too anxious and too guilty to say what he planned.
He never really planned to apologise in the first place.

feedback.es: Tras diez minutos de dudas y una disculpa ensayada, quedarse en blanco muestra que la inquietud y la culpa lo superan.

origin.audio: Leo waited outside his sister's door for ten minutes. He raised his hand, lowered it, and stared at the handle as if it might bite. Two weeks earlier he had sold her old guitar without asking, and he had rehearsed his apology all the way home. When the door finally opened, Sara simply looked at him, and he forgot every word he had prepared.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su significado en el relato.

feedback.es: Cada verbo o adjetivo muestra un ánimo distinto: quitar importancia, dudar, sentir vergüenza y temer.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo se siente Sara en realidad.

choices.text: Relieved, so she forgives him at once and completely.
Calm, since she was too busy with the guests to mind.
Hurt, although she hides it and stays polite.

feedback.es: Sonríe, mira la puerta cada pocos minutos y responde con frialdad: está dolida y lo disimula con cortesía.

origin.audio: Leo had promised to come early. By seven the guests were arriving, and there was still no sign of him. Sara kept smiling, filling glasses and answering questions, but every few minutes she looked at the door. When he finally appeared, pale and apologetic, she only said, don't worry about it, and turned back to the cake.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué mira Sara la puerta cada pocos minutos.

choices.text: She fears that Leo may not come at all.
She wants to see whether more guests are arriving.
She is waiting for someone to deliver the cake.

feedback.es: Leo prometió llegar pronto y no aparece: mira la puerta porque teme que no vaya a venir.

origin.audio: Leo had promised to come early. By seven the guests were arriving, and there was still no sign of him. Sara kept smiling, filling glasses and answering questions, but every few minutes she looked at the door. When he finally appeared, pale and apologetic, she only said, don't worry about it, and turned back to the cake.

prompt.es: Completa: «Intentó quitarle importancia a su disculpa con una broma.»

feedback.es: Brush off significa quitar importancia: intenta restar peso a la disculpa, pero su voz la delata.

origin.text: She tried to ___ off his apology with a joke, but her voice sounded tight and her smile did not reach her eyes.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué actitud muestra Carlos hacia la carta?

choices.text: He has already read it and feels relieved by what it says.
He puts off facing it because he dreads what it may say.
He is eager to answer it but has no paper to write on.

feedback.es: Pasa junto a la carta, se ocupa de otras cosas y se dice que puede esperar: la evita porque teme su contenido.

origin.text: The letter had been open on the table for three days. Carlos walked past it, moved the papers next to it, and made himself a coffee he did not want. Whatever it said, it could wait, he decided; it had waited long enough.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué sugiere el final sobre cómo es la abuela?

choices.text: That she is too proud to accept any excuse from Sara.
That she no longer expects Sara to visit her at all.
That she is kind enough not to demand an explanation.

feedback.es: Sara ensaya excusas, pero sabe que su abuela nunca las pediría: la abuela es comprensiva.

origin.text: Sara felt guilty all week. She had promised to help her grandmother move, then cancelled at the last minute for a party she hardly enjoyed. Now she kept rehearsing excuses, although she knew her grandmother would never ask for one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando la profesora preguntaba, Leo solía dudar un momento.»

feedback.es: Hesitate significa dudar: la pausa antes de responder muestra su inseguridad.

origin.text: Whenever the teacher asked a question, Leo would ___ for a moment before he answered, as if he feared a mistake.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué revela la voz demasiado alegre.

choices.text: That he is anxious and is trying to hide it.
That he is happy to hear from his mother.
That he is eager to share some good news.

feedback.es: Evita el teléfono, mira la pantalla y contesta con un tono forzado: está inquieto y lo disimula.

origin.audio: He had told everyone he was fine, yet he avoided the phone all afternoon. When it finally rang, he stared at the screen for a long moment before answering in a voice that was almost too cheerful. It was only his mother, and he let out a long breath.
